audit.why: Lane is Qiyana-favored at every stage (TF has no dash, one telegraphed stun); both layers agree on a 7/7 Qiyana chart. The 47.83% WR (1382 games) is the packet's flagged contradiction — it reflects Destiny map pressure after lane, not lane stages, so the chart is defensible and both layers already agree; left alone, noted for the user.
Qiyana spikes 3 (W-E-Q all-in on a dashless target), 6 (wall-pin R), first item (full-HP burst). TF's real spike is 6 Destiny for roams, not duels. spikes[] covers all four.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no numbers; Pick a Card's auto-reset tell (missing-interaction flag) was unstated; 'global Rick' typo in spikes[3].text; two copy-paste-bleed bullets. suspectNames flagged 'Gold Card (Pick a Card)' but that is correct usage — false positive, not changed.
audit.why: TF: W 6s (auto reset — wind-up is the tell), Q 6s at rank 1, Destiny 170/140/110s, E is a passive. Qiyana R 120s pins him with no escape.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns rewritten with numbers, auto-reset tell added to dosFull[0].d, typo fixed, bleed bullets replaced.

edits.before: Grass Q from the river brush line — the stealth-empowered poke chunks and the lane learns to fear hedges.
edits.after: He has no combat pressure at 1 — empowered-auto him off every Wild Cards cast and take the first push for free.

edits.before: W element economy begins: ice for the trades, rock for the executes, grass for the angles.
edits.after: Ice for the trade is optional — he cannot dodge much; hold W to sidestep the second Wild Cards.

edits.before: E joins: the stick-dash into ice-Q root is your first real kill pattern — pick one window per wave.
edits.after: W-E-Q assembled: he has no dash, so once the gold card is baited the all-in is close to guaranteed.

edits.before: Element-cycle the trades: E-ice-Q roots, auto, rock-Q the execute line. The lane is a terrain quiz.
edits.after: Each Gold Card he burns on the wave opens a 6-second kill window — your threat compounds every wave.

edits.before: Supreme Display online — any fight near a wall is a stun lottery you rigged. Hug terrain like rent depends on it.
edits.after: Supreme Display pins him to a wall with no escape tool — a mispositioned Twisted Fate at 6 is a guaranteed pickup.

edits.before: First item spike: the full element string deletes squishies. Force the brush-line fights.
edits.after: First item you burst him from full — he builds no armor, so one rotation ends the trade.

edits.before: Late Qiyana flanks through her own R: shockwave the objective wall, string the stunned, and vanish into grass.
edits.after: You still one-combo him, but Destiny roams decide the game — shove and follow rather than farming the lane.

edits.before: - Twisted Fate Pick a Card (Gold): matchup-defining — The locked gold card starts every trade and gank — back off the moment it glows yellow. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Terrashape (element swap) has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Twisted Fate Pick a Card (W): 6s — the locked gold card starts every trade and gank; back off the moment it glows yellow, commit the moment it's spent. - Wild Cards: 6s poke — sidestep it, never tank it. - Destiny: 170s at rank 1 — his roams live on it; ping the timer. - Your own R is 120s: hold it for the wall pin.

edits.before: The locked gold card starts every trade and gank — back off the moment it glows yellow. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Pick a Card is an auto reset — the card lock plus attack wind-up is the tell; step back on yellow, commit on its 6s downtime.

edits.before: Grass-Q from stealth, E-ice the answer, auto, walk back into the hedge — terrain trades he experiences as ambush weather.
edits.after: After he burns the gold stun on the wave or a bad trade, E on instantly — his W is 6s but he has no dash to answer you.

edits.before: E-ing in with no element loaded and his CC banked — Qiyana without terrain prep is a dagger doing improv.
edits.after: Rock Q bonus damage scales on missing health — open with brush or ice, save the rock for the sub-half execute.

edits.before: Grass-Q from stealth, E-ice the answer, auto, walk back into the hedge — terrain trades he experiences as ambush weather.
edits.after: Grass-Q from brush stealth, E, auto, W out before his 6s W is back — he has no dash to answer any part of the string.

edits.before: E-ing in with no element loaded and his CC banked — Qiyana without terrain prep is a dagger doing improv.
edits.after: E-ing into a held gold card — your E sticks to its target and the stun lands before your Q leaves your hands.

edits.before: Good trade: Grass-Q from stealth, E-ice the answer, auto, walk back into the hedge — terrain trades he experiences as ambush weather. Bad trade: E-ing in with no element loaded and his CC banked — Qiyana without terrain prep is a dagger doing improv.
edits.after: Good trade: Grass-Q from brush stealth, E, auto, W out before his 6s W is back — he has no dash to answer any part of the string. Bad trade: E-ing into a held gold card — your E sticks to its target and the stun lands before your Q leaves your hands.

edits.before: Twisted Fate wins by landing Pick a Card (Gold), denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Twisted Fate wins by shoving with Wild Cards and Destiny-gating to a sidelane — he beats you on the map, not in the lane.

edits.before: Lane stays yours, but respect Destiny — his level-6 global Rick means he roams sidelanes and other lanes. Ping his ult timer and shove-then-follow rather than overstaying to farm.
edits.after: Lane stays yours, but respect Destiny — his level-6 global ult means he roams for sidelane picks. Ping his ult timer and shove-then-follow rather than overstaying to farm.
